title: Neural Stem Cell Culture: Neurosphere generation, microscopical analysis and cryopreservation
protocol: Set the water bath to 37°C.
Bubble the tissue dissection solution with 95% O₂ and 5% CO₂ for 10 minutes.
Disinfect the dissection area with 95% ethanol.
Sterilize the dissection instruments in an antiseptic solution \(Cidex, followed by a complete sterile water rinse and then immerse in 95% ethanol).
Fill three 60 x 15 mm tissue culture dishes with 3.0 ml of the tissue dissection solution.
Euthanize the mouse in the CO₂ chamber.
Shave the top of the head.
Swab the head with gauze soaked in Betadine to sterilize and remove any loose hairs from the skin.
Swab the head with gauze soaked in 95% ethanol.
Make a midline incision in the skin with a scalpel blade over the entire length of the skull.
Reveal the surface of the skull by reflecting the skin.
Make additional cuts in the skin to expose the sides of the skull just below the ears.
Cut the skull on both sides with small scissors.
Break off the skull with forceps.
Slide curved forceps under the base of the brain to cut the spinal cord, blood vessels, and cranial nerves connected to the base of the brain.
Transfer the brain with the same curved forceps to a 60 mm tissue culture dish with dissection solution.
Strip any remaining meninges from the surface of the brain.
Rinse the brain thoroughly.
Place the brain into a second 60 mm tissue culture dish with dissection fluid.
Cut the brain along the midline under the dissecting scope.
Isolate the desired region of the brain with fine forceps.
Transfer the dissected tissue into a third 60 mm tissue culture dish containing tissue dissection solution.
Cut the tissue into small squares (approximately 1.0 mm³) with No. 10 curved scalpel blades.
Transfer the dish with the dissected tissue (small squares) to the tissue culture hood.
Load the tissue pieces into a 5 ml polypropylene round bottom tube using a Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 250g.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Add the enzyme mix (1.0 ml).
Place the tube in the water bath for at least 40 minutes (newborn to one week old) or approximately 1.5 hours (young adult less than 2 months old).
Triturate the samples briefly with a Pasteur pipette every 20 minutes during incubation.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 250g and remove the supernatant.
Add 4.0 ml of the trypsin inhibitor.
Triturate (10 times) with a Pasteur pipette to break up the pellet, minimizing air bubbles introduction.
Place the tube in the water bath for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 500g and remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cells in 0.5 ml of SFM.
Triturate sufficiently to produce a single cell suspension.
Calculate and adjust the viable cell concentration with a hemacytometer.
Determine viable cells by Trypan Blue dye exclusion.
Add 0.5 ml of SFM containing the cells to each well of a 24 multi-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C with 95% air and 5% CO₂.
Transfer the neurospheres and medium from all wells to a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 200g.
Remove the supernatant and add 2.0 ml of TrypLE<sup>TM</sup> to the tube.
Use a Pasteur pipette to mix the neurospheres with the TrypLE<sup>TM</sup>.
Place the tube in the water bath for 20 minutes at 37°C.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 500g.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend the cells in 0.5 ml of SFM.
Triturate with a Pasteur pipette (60-70 times).
Determine the cell concentration by Trypan Blue dye exclusion.
Plate the desired concentration of cells to a new 24 multi-well plate.
Incubate at 37°C with 95% air and 5% CO<sub>2</sub>.
Pool the culture medium with the neurospheres from a 24 multi-well plate into a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 200g.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend the cells in 10.0 ml SFM (without EGF and FGF) containing 15.0% dimethyl-sulfoxide (DMSO).
Gently mix the neurospheres in the SFM with a Pasteur pipette.
Aliquot 1.5 ml of the mixture into polypropylene cryovials (Nunc Cryo Tubes cat. no. 357418).
Transfer the tubes to a -80°C freezer overnight.
Transfer vials to a liquid nitrogen cryofreezer.
Let the vial warm up to room temperature on the bench when ready to re-establish neurospheres.
Add the contents of the cryovial slowly to a 15 ml conical tube containing 10 ml of SFM.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 200g and remove the supernatant.
Gently mix the neurospheres with 4.0 ml of the SFM using a Pasteur pipette.
Fill 8 wells of a 24 multi-well plate with 0.5 ml of the mixture.
Incubate at 37°C with 95% air and 5% CO₂.
Transfer the culture medium with neurospheres to a 50 ml polypropylene conical tube.
Allow the neurospheres to settle by gravity for approximately 30 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and mix gently with 2.0 ml of 4.0% phosphate buffered paraformaldehyde.
Allow the neurospheres to settle in the tube.
Remove the fixative supernatant using a Pasteur pipette and rinse with 5.0 ml of phosphate buffered saline.
Allow the neurospheres to settle for at least 30 minutes before removing the PBS.
Repeat the rinsing procedure at least three times.
Add 5.0 ml of 30% sucrose dissolved in 0.1M PBS.
Transfer the tube to the fridge and allow the neurospheres to settle overnight.
Remove the 30% sucrose and add embedding medium for frozen tissue specimens for 1 hour.
Prepare the cryostat chuck with a layer of O.C.T.
Transfer the neurosphere pellet to the O.C.T. layer on the cryostat chuck using a Pasteur pipette or an Eppendorf pipettor pre-loaded with a small amount of O.C.T.
Cut sections at desired thickness and collect on APTEX coated glass microscope slides.
Continue with the desired immunocytochemical procedure, including non-specific blocking and application of primary antibody.
